**Unofficial** integration, not affiliated with P1 Monitor (ztatz). It reads
**P1 Monitor**, the software (often on a Raspberry Pi) plugged into the P1
port of your smart meter (Belgium, Netherlands), **through its local API**,
without any cloud or account.

> **Never tested with a real P1 Monitor.** The integration was written from
> the p1monitor library (used by Home Assistant) and simulated answers. Your
> feedback on the Gladys forum is welcome.

### This is not…

- the **DSMR Reader** integration (by GBoulvin), which reads another
  software, DSMR Reader;
- the **YouLess** integration, which reads the YouLess box;
- the **HomeWizard** integration, which reads the HomeWizard box (P1 Meter).

Use the one that matches what is plugged into your meter: two of them on the
same meter would count the consumption twice in the energy monitoring.

## What you get

One "P1 Monitor" device, with only what your meter gives:

| Value                                                     | Pace   | Type in Gladys                                  |
| --------------------------------------------------------- | ------ | ----------------------------------------------- |
| Power taken from the grid (W)                             | 10 s   | energy sensor, power                            |
| Power injected into the grid (W)                          | 10 s   | plain sensor                                    |
| Consumption index (kWh): low tariff + high tariff         | 1 min  | energy sensor, **index**: energy monitoring     |
| Consumption index per tariff, low and high (kWh)          | 1 min  | plain sensors                                   |
| Injection index, total and per tariff (kWh)               | 1 min  | plain sensors, **never billed**                 |
| Current tariff (1 = low, 2 = high)                        | 1 min  | plain sensor                                    |
| Per phase: power taken and injected (W), voltage, current | 10 s   | sensors without history by default              |
| Gas (m³)                                                  | 1 min  | volume sensor, **out of the energy monitoring** |
| Water (m³), when a water meter is wired to P1 Monitor     | 5 min  | volume sensor, **out of the energy monitoring** |
| Prices set in P1 Monitor (€/kWh, €/m³)                    | 15 min | plain sensors                                   |

The Gladys **energy monitoring** derives the consumption per half hour and
its cost from the consumption index by itself (low + high tariff of the
meter, two cumulative counters: never a daily total, never the injection).
Injection, gas and water stay apart: Gladys would price gas at the
electricity tariff, and the injection would be counted as a consumption. The
P1 Monitor prices are only shown: the cost in Gladys comes from your Gladys
energy contracts.

"Low tariff" and "high tariff" are the names P1 Monitor uses (`LOW` and
`HIGH`, "dal" and "piek"; tariff code `D` or `P`). On a Belgian meter, where
tariff 1 is the day tariff, check which one matches your bill (not verified).

## Installation

1. Preferably give the device running P1 Monitor a **fixed IP address** in
   your router. If it changes, enter the new one: the Gladys device (one per
   integration) and its history are kept.
2. In Gladys, install the P1 Monitor integration from the store, open its
   configuration and enter the **address** (e.g. `192.168.1.40`, with
   `:port` only if it is not 80).
3. Click **Test the connection**: the power and index read are shown.
4. In the **Discover** tab, create the P1 Monitor device. The values arrive
   at once.

The API is read over plain HTTP on your network, without a password (as Home
Assistant does); the HTTPS of P1 Monitor is not used.

## Good to know

- **P1 Monitor unreachable**: the integration status says so, and it tries
  again after 10 s, then 20 s, 40 s… up to 5 minutes, never giving up. Saving
  the configuration tries again at once.
- **Secondary pages** (phases, prices, water meter) failing: the power and
  the indexes go on; the status says so, and the page is tried again every
  5 minutes. Without a water meter, the water page is asked again only once
  an hour (a meter added later appears).
- **Frozen reading**: when P1 Monitor gives the same meter reading for
  5 minutes (P1 cable unplugged, reading stopped), the power and the phases
  are no longer sent (they would look current) and the status says so.
- **Consumption index protected** (Gladys counts every rise in full):
  - an index at 0 is never sent, nor a partial sum: a tariff missing, a
    tariff that was above 0 and reads 0, or a single tariff dropping give no
    index for that reading (a register glitching is not a drop). The tariff
    and injection indexes, gas and water are never sent at 0 either;
  - a **drop** of both tariffs (meter replaced or reset) is **never**
    accepted by itself, not by time either: it is held, the last accepted
    value is sent again to Gladys, and the integration status shows it. If
    the values come back, they go on normally, without any fictive kWh;
  - a **jump up** (more than 100 kW on average since the last accepted
    value) is not accepted by itself, not by repetition, not by time: every
    value at or above it stays held (the hold is kept in `/data` across a
    restart), the last accepted value is sent again to Gladys, and the
    status shows the jump, even while the P1 Monitor is unreachable;
  - to accept a held value, click **Accept the held index** in the
    configuration of the integration, **twice**. The first click accepts
    nothing: it answers with the value held and what will be counted. The
    second click, after a few seconds and within 5 minutes, accepts
    **exactly that value** (plus what the home may use meanwhile): for a
    jump, the difference (for instance 5000 kWh) **will be counted at once
    as consumption**, accept only if this energy was really consumed; for a
    drop, nothing is billed and the consumption goes on from there. The
    normal consumption of the home between the two clicks is accepted with
    it; if a value beyond what the home may have used was read between the
    two clicks, nothing is accepted: click again to see it. Another value read afterwards stays held.
    **Saving the configuration never accepts anything**;
  - the margin counts time on the integration's own clock (the time elapsed
    since it started): the clock of the machine set by hours (NTP, a
    Raspberry Pi without a battery-backed clock) widens nothing while the
    integration runs, and a date ahead of the clock counts as now. Two rare
    cases remain: an integration that **starts** with the clock hours ahead
    may let a glitch through (100 kWh per hour of error) as long as the
    index has not moved since its start (for instance during solar export),
    and so may the next start after a restart within a minute of the clock
    being set. After a long stop of the machine (sleep) or a start without
    the time, a real rise may be held: accept it with the button;
  - if a register stays stuck (for instance a new meter with a tariff staying
    at 0 when it was not) and the status keeps saying "no index", the way
    out is to **delete the device and create it again** from the Discover
    tab: its reference starts again;
  - the 100 kW margin counts from the last accepted value: after a long
    outage it grows (24 hours of outage let up to 2400 kWh through at once).
    A frozen reading (same value) does not move the date of the last value,
    so that the recovery is not taken for a jump.
- Unchanged values are sent again only every 10 minutes; on each
  reconnection to Gladys, the device, all its values and the status are
  published again.
- The features of the device are fixed when it is created: if a value
  appears later (first solar panels, a water meter), click "Update" in the
  Discover tab: the new values arrive at once. The device published again
  never loses a feature of the created one, even if a value is missing for a
  while.
- The injection (power, indexes, injection prices) appears only once it is
  above 0: a home without panels does not see these values.

## Limits

- One P1 Monitor per installation of the integration.
- The dynamic tariffs and the history of P1 Monitor are not read.
- No protected access (password, HTTPS): the local API must be reachable
  over HTTP from Gladys.

## Parámetros de configuración

Estos son los parámetros que P1 Monitor te pide en su pantalla de configuración en Gladys.

| Parámetro | Tipo | Obligatorio | Descripción |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| P1 Monitor | `section` | No | Unofficial connector, not affiliated with P1 Monitor (ztatz). It reads your P1 Monitor, the software plugged into the P1 port of your smart meter (Belgium, Netherlands), through its local API, without any cloud: the power taken and injected every 10 seconds, the electricity index every minute for the Gladys energy monitoring, and, when the meter gives them, the indexes per tariff, the injection, the phases, gas, water and the prices set in P1 Monitor. Gas and water are plain sensors in m³: they stay out of the energy monitoring. Not the DSMR Reader, YouLess or HomeWizard integrations. Never tested with a real P1 Monitor. |
| P1 Monitor address | `string` | Sí | The IP address of the device running P1 Monitor on your network (shown by your router), with a port only if it is not 80. Preferably give it a fixed address in your router; if it changes, enter the new one: the device and its history are kept. |

## Cómo instalar P1 Monitor en Gladys

1. En Gladys, abre **Integraciones**: P1 Monitor aparece en el catálogo junto a las integraciones nativas, con una insignia de comunidad.
2. Haz clic en **Instalar**. Gladys descarga la imagen Docker (`ghcr.io/lm1lc3n7/gladys-p1-monitor:0.1.5`), la ejecuta en un entorno aislado del núcleo y genera la interfaz de la integración (dispositivos, descubrimiento y configuración).
3. Abre la pantalla de **Configuración** de la integración, rellena los parámetros y guarda.
4. También puedes instalarla directamente desde la URL de su repositorio: [https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-p1-monitor](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-p1-monitor).

P1 Monitor requiere Gladys `>=5.2.0`. El catálogo de Gladys se actualiza cada hora, así que una nueva versión está disponible como máximo una hora después de publicarse.

¿Todavía no usas Gladys? Es gratuito y de código abierto: [sigue la guía de instalación](/es/docs/) para empezar.

## Sobre las integraciones externas

P1 Monitor es una **integración externa**: una integración comunitaria empaquetada como contenedor Docker y publicada en GitHub. Gladys la instala con un clic y la ejecuta en un entorno aislado del núcleo. La publica y mantiene [LM1LC3N7](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7), no el equipo principal de Gladys.
